topic.subject: science
topic.title: Soil
topic.scope: soil profile and horizons, types of soil, percolation, water retention, soil and crops, soil erosion

misconceptions.statement: Soil is just dirt or dead matter with no living components.
misconceptions.why: Students often focus only on the mineral particles they see and ignore the microscopic life.
misconceptions.fix: Soil is a complex mixture of weathered rock particles, minerals, organic matter (humus), air, water, and living organisms like bacteria and earthworms.

probe.question: Is soil a living or non-living thing?
probe.wrong_answer: It is non-living because it is just ground-up rock.

misconceptions.statement: Soil is created instantly by mixing sand and water.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the physical act of mixing materials with the geological process of soil formation.
misconceptions.fix: Soil formation is a very slow process taking thousands of years, involving the breakdown of rocks by wind, water, and climate.

probe.question: How long does it take for a layer of soil to form?
probe.wrong_answer: It happens quickly whenever rocks break down or get wet.

misconceptions.statement: All soil layers are the same throughout the ground.
misconceptions.why: Students often see only the top layer and assume it is uniform all the way down to the bedrock.
misconceptions.fix: Soil is arranged in distinct layers called horizons (A, B, C, and bedrock), which differ in color, texture, and composition.

probe.question: If you dig a deep hole, will the soil at the bottom be the same as the top?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, soil is the same all the way down.

misconceptions.statement: Sandy soil is the best soil for all plants because it is loose.
misconceptions.why: Students associate 'loose' soil with 'easy' root growth, ignoring water retention needs.
misconceptions.fix: Different plants need different soils; sandy soil drains too quickly for many crops, while loamy soil is often best because it balances water retention and aeration.

probe.question: Which soil is best for growing wheat?
probe.wrong_answer: Sandy soil, because it is loose and easy for roots to move through.

misconceptions.statement: Water disappears from soil because it is absorbed by the soil particles themselves.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the physical process of water moving through spaces (percolation) with the chemical absorption of water into the material.
misconceptions.fix: Water percolates through the spaces between soil particles; the rate depends on the size of these spaces, not the absorption by the particles.

probe.question: Where does water go when it percolates through sandy soil?
probe.wrong_answer: The soil particles soak it up like a sponge.
